reviewer_notes: Replaces the 2022 to 2023 utility-scale solar moratorium (Sabin REC-0118, held back as lifted; last set to expire Sept. 30, 2023). Ordinance: repeal and replace of Linn County Code ch. 107 (Unified Development Code), art. VI, sec. 107-117(h) 'Utilities, Utility Scale Solar Installations', county case PA23-0007. Ordinance text (prepared by Linn County Planning & Development): https://www.cleanenergydistricts.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/Linn-County-Utility-Scale-Solar-Siting-Ordinance.pdf ; county page: https://www.linncountyiowa.gov/1525/Utility-Scale-Solar ; county release: https://www.linncountyiowa.gov/CivicAlerts.aspx?AID=3367 ; Gazette: https://www.thegazette.com/local-government/government-notes-linn-county-supervisors-pass-solar-ordinance/ . Adopted: Planning and Zoning Commission Aug. 16, 2023; Board of Supervisors readings Sept. 5, 13 and 20, 2023, final passage unanimous Sept. 20, 2023; effective on publication in The Gazette (date not found). Setbacks: panels, structures and electrical equipment 300 ft from dwellings unless the owner waives it in writing (recorded); 50 ft from property lines; battery storage 200 ft from a property line or right-of-way; 120 ft from the centerline of perennial streams and ditches. Acreage caps: none found (no county-wide, farmland-share or per-project cap). CSR2: no ban; land rated 65 CSR or above is discouraged through a scorecard that projects must pass (approved 2-1). Also: rezoning to the RE overlay district, panels at least 24 in. above ground, vegetative screening for dwellings within 1,000 ft, decommissioning cost recalculated every five years, 55 dBA daytime noise limit. Does not apply to previously approved projects. Severity 2 by the README rule (solar setback under 1,000 ft). Not found: ordinance number, Gazette publication date, any 2024 to 2026 solar amendment. Every fact above was seen in search-index text; no page was opened because this session's network policy blocked linncountyiowa.gov and the news hosts. Open the minutes and the ordinance text to verify.
description: Linn County replaced its utility-scale solar moratorium with siting rules in its Unified Development Code: panels 300 ft from dwellings unless the owner waives it, 50 ft from property lines, battery storage 200 ft from property lines and rights-of-way, RE overlay rezoning and a passing score on the county's solar scorecard. No acreage cap.
evidence_text: Solar panels, structures, and electrical equipment, excluding fences and power lines for interconnection, shall be kept a minimum of three hundred (300) feet from dwellings, unless the property owner waives the setback. Waiver must be in writing and recorded.
